No. Do not append passes to that log and call the revised draft checked.

Why not

- The log is bound to the exact bytes of the draft, the sources, and a canonical-JSON hash of the inventory. When the draft or the inventory changes, the old log is stale. The helper treats that as malformed or stale evidence (exit status 2) and will not accept new entries against it.
- Each pass in the old log only shows what was true of the old draft and old inventory. A pass recorded for a quotation, pincite, or proposition as it stood before the edit says nothing about the revised wording. The revision may have changed a quote, moved a pincite, added or dropped a citation use, or changed the proposition a case is cited for.
- Appending new passes to the old log would also mix evidence from two different drafts in one record. The tool allows one record per use and check, and one writer per run. Contradictory or replacement entries are not allowed to bury an earlier result. Editing the log by hand to get around this is not detected by the helper. It would produce a record that looks clean but is not trustworthy.
- "Checked" has a defined meaning here. It means that every required check for every citation use in the final revised draft has passing evidence recorded against that draft. A log from the earlier draft cannot show that.

Next step

I have not run any tools or looked at your files, so I can't tell you which old results would carry over. Here is what to do.

1. Preserve the old run as it is. Keep the old inventory, `checks.jsonl`, and report unchanged, and do not edit them.
2. Fix the final draft. Do the new verification against the revised draft you intend to file or send. If you will edit it again, wait. Any further change will require another run.
3. Rebuild the inventory by hand from the revised draft. Include every use: full and short citations, `id.` chains, footnotes, quotations, string cites, statutes, regulations, rules, and record cites. Give separate uses to different propositions, locators, and short forms. Mark each unpublished Wisconsin Court of Appeals opinion with `"unpublished_wis_ct_app": true`, which adds a citability check under Wis. Stat. § 809.23(3). Then compute `document_sha256` from the revised draft's exact bytes.
4. Start new files: a new inventory, a new `checks.jsonl`, and a new report path. The tool never overwrites an existing report.
5. Re-record the evidence for the new run. For each use, record the required checks (`citation`, `pincite`, `treatment`, `proposition`, `format`, plus `verbatim` for a quote, `citability` for an unpublished Wisconsin Court of Appeals opinion, and `record` in place of the authority checks for record cites). Set `provenance_origin` on every entry.
   - Use the archived sources again where the source bytes have not changed. The hash and locator still have to match. Re-read the source for any use whose quote, pincite, or proposition changed. If a source file changed, that also requires a new run.
   - A `remembered` origin cannot pass any check.
   - Do not copy an old pass forward by assumption. If a use is textually identical and its source is unchanged, you can re-enter the evidence for it, but enter it in the new log, not the old one.
6. Run the report against the new inventory and log. `RECORDED PASS` appears only when every required check for every use has passing evidence. Anything missing shows as `UNVERIFIED`, and anything failed shows as `FLAGGED`. A report that generates successfully is not a pass. Check the status, not just the exit.
7. Report honestly. If a case's treatment was screened only with free sources (for example, a CourtListener citing-cases scan), the best result is `caution` ("no citator run"), not a pass. Say so at the conclusion. Only a named citator run can support `pass` on treatment.

If you cannot run Python or write files in your environment, you can do the same review manually. Label it a manual report, give a source and locator for each check, and do not imply that scripted checks ran.

What you can say now

You can describe the revised draft as "not yet verified; prior check results apply to an earlier version" until the new run is complete. Even a complete run is a review aid. It is not an independent legal judgment, and it is not permission to file. A lawyer or the filer still has to decide whether the draft is ready.

If you want, send me the revised draft, the new inventory, and the sources you have for it, and I can help you build the inventory and review the quotes and propositions against the supplied text. I have no way to browse, run a citator, or run the script from here, so treat any result I give you as limited to what you provide.
